speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, are you currently pregnant, and if so, how many weeks along are you? This is critical given your symptoms of vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain.

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information, Ms. Smith. Given your history of a prior cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe abdominal pain followed by bleeding at 38 weeks, I am concerned about uterine rupture. Have you experienced any sudden loss of fetal movement or a sensation that the baby has moved away from the abdominal wall?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture

REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_pelvis_and_vagina to assess fetal position and free fluid, and Fetal_ECG for heart rate monitoring.
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count and Coagulation_Profile immediately.
